# Mission: Complete Reverse Engineering, Strategic Product Analysis & Ground-Up Reconstruction of LarkPlayer.com as the Official Weechy Website

## 1. YOUR MISSION

You are being assigned a complete product research, competitive analysis, website architecture, UX engineering, visual design, and full-stack implementation mission.

Your task is to independently investigate **https://larkplayer.com/** in its entirety, understand what makes it work, identify its features, structure, design decisions, interactions, content strategy, and technical behavior, and then use those findings as a foundation to build an entirely new website from scratch under the identity of **Weechy**.

This is NOT a simple redesign.
This is NOT a theme replacement.
This is NOT a logo replacement.
This is NOT a request to reproduce Lark Player with different colors.

The objective is to create a complete, polished, modern, highly functional, production-quality website that uses the strongest ideas and useful capabilities discovered during your investigation while establishing an entirely independent Weechy identity.

The final result must feel like a real, professionally developed product website, not a generic AI-generated landing page.

You are responsible for performing the research yourself. Do not ask me to explain Lark Player, describe its pages, or provide screenshots of its functionality unless access limitations make something genuinely impossible to investigate.

---

# 2. THE TWO PRIMARY SOURCES OF TRUTH

You have two essential sources to work with.

### SOURCE A — Lark Player

Website:
https://larkplayer.com/

You must investigate the actual website directly.

Do not rely exclusively on search engine descriptions, third-party articles, or assumptions about what a music player website should contain.

Explore the website as a real visitor would.

### SOURCE B — Weechy Complete Technical Reference

File:
`APP_COMPLETE_REFERENCE.md`

This file is already available in the project environment.

You MUST read the entire document carefully, from beginning to end, including:

- Application identity and product positioning.
- Architecture and internal components.
- All application screens.
- Music playback capabilities.
- Local music library management.
- Queue and playlist functionality.
- Lyrics architecture.
- Equalizer and audio amplification.
- Animations and gesture systems.
- Settings and preferences.
- Dialogs and interactions.
- Update infrastructure.
- Data models and storage.
- Android integrations.
- Visual assets and design system.
- External services.
- Error handling.
- Complete feature matrix.
- Website-relevant product information.

Treat this document as the authoritative reference for what Weechy actually is and what the Android application actually supports.

Do not invent features simply because they would make the website appear more impressive.

If a feature is mentioned in the documentation but its actual implementation or availability is unclear, investigate the distinction before presenting it as a confirmed capability.

---

# 3. PHASE ONE — COMPLETE LARK PLAYER INVESTIGATION

Before designing or implementing anything, perform a systematic investigation of Lark Player's website.

Your research must be comprehensive.

## 3.1 Website Structure and Information Architecture

Identify every publicly accessible page and meaningful section.

Investigate:

- Homepage.
- Navigation system.
- Header and footer.
- Product pages.
- Feature pages.
- Download pages.
- About sections.
- Support and help sections.
- FAQ.
- Legal and policy pages.
- Blog or news sections, if present.
- Contact and social links.
- Any additional pages discovered during exploration.

Build a complete internal sitemap.

Identify how visitors move between pages and how the website organizes its information.

## 3.2 Visual Design Investigation

Study the website's visual language in detail.

Examine:

- Overall visual identity.
- Color palette.
- Typography.
- Font weights and hierarchy.
- Background treatments.
- Navigation appearance.
- Buttons and their states.
- Cards and containers.
- Borders and shadows.
- Spacing system.
- Grid structures.
- Image composition.
- Illustrations.
- Product screenshots.
- Iconography.
- Decorative elements.
- Responsive behavior.
- Desktop and mobile layouts.

Pay attention to how individual components work together rather than evaluating them independently.

## 3.3 Functional Investigation

Do not stop at looking at screenshots.

Actually interact with the website wherever possible.

Test:

- Navigation links.
- Dropdown menus.
- Buttons.
- Download actions.
- Language selectors.
- Tabs.
- Accordions.
- Animations.
- Scroll-triggered effects.
- Mobile menus.
- Forms.
- Search functionality.
- Interactive demonstrations.
- External integrations.
- Responsive navigation.
- Hover and focus states.

Determine which elements are genuinely functional and which are merely decorative.

Record important interactions and their behavior.

## 3.4 Content and Marketing Investigation

Analyze how Lark Player communicates its product.

Understand:

- Its primary value proposition.
- Its target audience.
- Its marketing language.
- Its feature presentation.
- Its product screenshots.
- Its download conversion strategy.
- Its trust signals.
- Its calls to action.
- Its content hierarchy.
- Its SEO-oriented content.
- Its approach to explaining technical features to ordinary users.

Identify what is effective and what could be improved.

## 3.5 Technical and Performance Investigation

Investigate observable technical characteristics wherever possible.

Evaluate:

- Loading behavior.
- Image optimization.
- Responsive image handling.
- Navigation performance.
- Animation performance.
- Accessibility.
- Mobile usability.
- Page responsiveness.
- Metadata.
- SEO structure.
- Browser compatibility.
- Error states.
- External dependencies.

Do not claim to know inaccessible backend implementation details.

Distinguish observed facts from technical assumptions.

## 3.6 Competitive Opportunity Analysis

After completing the investigation, identify:

1. What Lark Player does particularly well.
2. What makes its website effective.
3. What feels outdated, unnecessary, confusing, or poorly organized.
4. What could be simplified.
5. What could be presented more elegantly.
6. What Weechy could communicate more effectively.
7. What opportunities exist to create a better overall experience.

The objective is not to copy Lark Player.

The objective is to understand its strengths, learn from its weaknesses, and build something better.

---

# 4. PHASE TWO — UNDERSTAND WEECHY AS A PRODUCT

Now connect your findings to the actual Weechy application documented in `APP_COMPLETE_REFERENCE.md`.

Weechy is a modern Android music player developed and owned by `itsmectrl`.

Its product identity is based on providing a sophisticated local music listening experience with powerful playback tools, carefully designed interactions, and a visually polished interface.

The website must communicate the actual product rather than presenting Weechy as a generic music application.

## 4.1 Core Product Capabilities

Use the documented capabilities as the foundation of the website's feature presentation.

### Music Library

- Local music library.
- Songs.
- Albums.
- Artists.
- Playlists.
- Folder-based browsing.
- Track management.
- Favorites.
- Music metadata.
- Album artwork handling.

### Advanced Music Playback

- Background playback.
- Media session integration.
- Playback notifications.
- Audio focus handling.
- Headphone disconnection behavior.
- Previous and next track controls.
- Repeat modes.
- Shuffle.
- Playback speed.
- Sleep timer.

### Advanced Audio System

One of Weechy's important differentiators is its audio amplification system.

Present its documented capabilities accurately:

- Up to 400% digital audio amplification.
- Android LoudnessEnhancer integration.
- Up to approximately +12.04 dB.
- Five-band equalizer.
- Multiple equalizer presets.
- Hearing safety warning above 150% amplification.

Never misrepresent the amplification as a guaranteed increase in hardware speaker output or as distortion-free under every condition.

### Synchronized Lyrics

Present:

- Embedded lyrics support.
- Local lyrics caching.
- LRCLIB integration.
- Synchronized LRC lyrics.
- Automatic active-line highlighting.
- Automatic lyrics scrolling.
- Tap-to-seek functionality.
- Lyrics retrieval and retry behavior.

### Customization

Present the actual customization capabilities:

- Light and dark themes.
- Accent color selection.
- Artwork-based dynamic player palette.
- Animated color transitions.
- Album artwork presentation options.

### Advanced Interaction Design

One of Weechy's distinguishing characteristics is its carefully engineered player interaction system.

Communicate the following:

- 1:1 vertical player sheet dragging.
- Fluid expansion and collapse behavior.
- Directionally arbitrated artwork swiping.
- Horizontal track skipping without interfering with vertical sheet gestures.
- Animated player transitions.
- Dynamic album-artwork-based colors.

These features deserve thoughtful visual presentation because they distinguish Weechy from an ordinary music player.

### Application Updates

Present the actual update ecosystem:

- GitHub-based releases.
- Update notifications.
- Automatic update checking.
- Version verification.
- Application identity protection.
- Backup export functionality when signature conflicts occur.

## 4.2 Product Accuracy Rules

The website is a presentation and distribution platform for an Android application.

Do not confuse website functionality with Android application functionality.

For example:

- Do not claim that the website can scan a visitor's Android music library.
- Do not claim that music playback happens directly inside the website.
- Do not promise cloud synchronization if it is not documented.
- Do not invent user accounts.
- Do not invent subscription plans.
- Do not invent streaming catalogs.
- Do not invent social features.
- Do not invent integrations.
- Do not invent privacy certifications.
- Do not claim that unsupported operating systems are officially supported.

Everything must be grounded in the actual product documentation.

You may create useful website features that support the product, provided they are clearly website features rather than falsely attributed Android application capabilities.

---

# 5. PHASE THREE — ESTABLISH THE COMPLETE WEECHY IDENTITY

The reconstructed website must belong entirely to Weechy.

Lark Player is the reference for research, not the identity to preserve.

## 5.1 Brand Identity

Official name: Weechy

Developer and copyright owner: itsmectrl

Product category: Android local music player.

Official application release:
https://github.com/itsmectrl/weechy-releases/releases/tag/new-version-4.1

The website must establish Weechy as an independent, recognizable product.

Use the existing Weechy identity, not a newly invented brand.

## 5.2 Visual Design Direction

Use the documented Weechy design system as the primary foundation.

Core colors:

- Background: `#09090C`
- Surface: `#14131A`
- Primary accent: `#E50914`

Build a refined dark visual environment around these colors.

The visual result should communicate:

- Precision.
- Simplicity.
- Sophistication.
- Modernity.
- Technical quality.
- Strong product identity.

Avoid:

- Generic AI landing page aesthetics.
- Excessive gradients.
- Unnecessary glassmorphism.
- Excessive rounded cards.
- Random decorative elements.
- Excessive animations.
- Oversized marketing text.
- Repetitive feature cards.
- Artificial-looking product screenshots.
- Unnecessary visual clutter.

Use red intentionally rather than applying it to everything.

The design must feel cohesive and professionally art-directed.

## 5.3 Artwork-Based Visual Language

Weechy has a dynamic palette engine that extracts colors from album artwork and smoothly interpolates the player interface between tracks.

Use this as an important visual storytelling opportunity.

Where appropriate, demonstrate how album artwork can influence the visual atmosphere of the player.

Create visually convincing product presentations that explain this capability.

Do not confuse a website's decorative demonstration with an actual running instance of the Android audio engine.

---

# 6. PHASE FOUR — DESIGN THE NEW WEECHY WEBSITE

Use everything learned from the investigation to create a complete website architecture.

Do not blindly reproduce Lark Player's sitemap.

Instead, determine the best information architecture for Weechy.

Consider the following possible sections, but make your own decisions based on the research and product requirements.

## 6.1 Homepage

The homepage must immediately communicate:

- What Weechy is.
- What makes it different.
- Why someone should consider installing it.
- Where to download it.
- Where to learn more.

It should have a strong visual introduction to the actual application.

Avoid a generic hero consisting of a headline, paragraph, and two ordinary buttons.

Design an original product presentation that makes Weechy's identity recognizable.

## 6.2 Product Features

Create a well-organized presentation of the real application capabilities.

Potential feature groups:

- Your music library.
- A more powerful listening experience.
- Advanced equalizer and amplification.
- Synchronized lyrics.
- Intelligent player interactions.
- Dynamic themes.
- Playback management.

Use appropriate visual demonstrations and actual application screenshots when available.

## 6.3 Product Experience

Present Weechy's actual application experience in a way that helps visitors understand the interface.

Possible presentations:

- Library interface.
- Expanded player.
- Lyrics interface.
- Equalizer.
- Queue management.
- Theme customization.

Use genuine available assets whenever possible.

Do not manufacture fake screenshots and represent them as actual application screenshots.

If real screenshots are unavailable, create clearly illustrative product demonstrations.

## 6.4 Download Experience

Create a clear and professional Android download experience.

Use the official release URL:

https://github.com/itsmectrl/weechy-releases/releases/tag/new-version-4.1

Display verified product information:

- Application name.
- Current documented version: 4.1.
- Android minimum requirement: Android 8.0.
- Download destination.
- Release information.

Do not invent download statistics, review counts, installation numbers, or compatibility claims.

## 6.5 About Weechy

Introduce Weechy as an independent software project developed by itsmectrl.

Explain its philosophy and approach to local music listening.

Maintain a professional, concise, product-focused tone.

## 6.6 Additional Useful Sections

Determine whether Weechy would benefit from:

- FAQ.
- Help and troubleshooting.
- Release history.
- Documentation.
- Contact information.
- Privacy information.
- Changelog.
- Feature comparison.
- Support information.

Only implement sections that make sense for the product.

Do not create empty pages or fake functionality merely to make the website appear larger.

---

# 7. PHASE FIVE — RECONSTRUCTION FROM ZERO

Once the research and architecture decisions are complete, implement the website.

This is a complete reconstruction task.

Do not simply modify Lark Player's existing visual structure.

Build an independent Weechy website with its own:

- Component architecture.
- Page structure.
- Design system.
- Navigation.
- Responsive layouts.
- Reusable components.
- Interactions.
- Animations.
- Content organization.
- Asset management.
- SEO implementation.

Inspect the existing project directory before making changes.

Understand its current framework, dependencies, configuration, and build environment.

Reuse suitable infrastructure where appropriate, but do not preserve unsuitable design or architecture merely because it already exists.

Avoid unnecessary dependencies.

Do not introduce a backend unless a real requirement justifies it.

Do not expose private credentials, tokens, or development information.

---

# 8. PHASE SIX — ENGINEERING AND FUNCTIONAL QUALITY

The result must be a working website, not just a static visual prototype.

## 8.1 Responsive Design

Implement and test:

- Large desktop screens.
- Standard desktop screens.
- Laptops.
- Tablets.
- Mobile phones.

Pay particular attention to mobile navigation, typography, product imagery, and content density.

No horizontal overflow.

No broken layouts.

No overlapping elements.

No inaccessible interactive controls.

## 8.2 Interaction Quality

Every interactive element must have a real, meaningful behavior.

Implement:

- Navigation.
- Dropdowns where needed.
- Mobile navigation.
- Functional buttons.
- Download links.
- Internal navigation.
- Expandable FAQ sections if included.
- Appropriate hover and focus states.
- Smooth but restrained transitions.

Never leave decorative buttons that do nothing.

Do not create fake loading indicators or fake success messages.

## 8.3 Performance

Optimize:

- Image sizes.
- Image formats.
- Asset loading.
- Font loading.
- Animation complexity.
- Component rendering.
- Page loading.
- Layout stability.

Avoid unnecessary JavaScript.

Prefer lightweight, maintainable solutions.

## 8.4 Accessibility

Ensure:

- Semantic HTML.
- Proper heading hierarchy.
- Keyboard navigation.
- Visible focus states.
- Accessible labels.
- Appropriate color contrast.
- Reduced-motion support.
- Correct image alternative text.

## 8.5 SEO and Metadata

Implement:

- Page titles.
- Meta descriptions.
- Open Graph metadata.
- Appropriate canonical URLs when the official domain is established.
- Sitemap where applicable.
- Robots configuration.
- Semantic content structure.
- Descriptive image metadata.

Do not invent an official domain if it has not been established.

---

# 9. PHASE SEVEN — QUALITY ASSURANCE

Do not consider the mission complete immediately after the first successful render.

Inspect and test the actual implementation.

Verify:

1. All intended pages load.
2. All navigation links work.
3. All download links lead to the correct destination.
4. No broken images exist.
5. No dead buttons remain.
6. No placeholder content remains.
7. No accidental Lark Player branding remains.
8. No references to unrelated products remain.
9. Mobile layouts work correctly.
10. Desktop layouts work correctly.
11. Browser console has no relevant errors.
12. The production build succeeds.
13. The design remains consistent across all pages.
14. Product claims match the Weechy documentation.

Run available automated checks and perform browser-based interaction testing.

Fix problems rather than merely reporting them.

---

# 10. IMPORTANT INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND ORIGINALITY REQUIREMENTS

Use Lark Player as a subject of research and competitive analysis.

Do not copy its proprietary source code, logos, brand assets, copyrighted illustrations, or unique visual assets.

Do not reproduce its branding.

Do not present Lark Player's features as Weechy features.

Create original implementations and original visual compositions.

The finished website must be unmistakably Weechy.

The copyright and developer identity must remain:

**© itsmectrl — Weechy. All rights reserved.**

Do not transfer ownership or invent additional copyright holders.

---

# 11. EXECUTION STRATEGY

Work through the following stages in order:

### Stage 1 — Research

Investigate Lark Player thoroughly.

Read the complete Weechy reference document.

Understand both products.

### Stage 2 — Analysis

Establish the sitemap, feature mapping, competitive opportunities, design direction, and implementation strategy.

Internally distinguish:

- Lark Player observations.
- Weechy documented capabilities.
- New website functionality.
- Design decisions.
- Unverified assumptions.

### Stage 3 — Architecture

Plan the new website's page structure, components, visual system, and technical implementation.

### Stage 4 — Implementation

Build the complete website from the ground up.

Do not stop after presenting a plan or mockup.

### Stage 5 — Testing

Run the website, inspect it, test its interactions, and fix identified problems.

### Stage 6 — Finalization

Deliver a complete working implementation.

---

# 12. FINAL EXPECTATION

I do not want a website that merely looks similar to Lark Player.

I want the result of a serious product investigation followed by an independent reconstruction.

Use Lark Player to understand what a successful music player website can offer.

Use the Weechy reference document to understand what Weechy actually offers.

Combine the useful discoveries into an entirely new, coherent product experience.

The final website should:

- Have a stronger and more distinctive identity.
- Communicate Weechy's actual capabilities more effectively.
- Present the application with beautiful and convincing product visuals.
- Have excellent information architecture.
- Feel sophisticated and carefully designed.
- Work exceptionally well on mobile and desktop.
- Have functional navigation and interactions.
- Be technically clean and maintainable.
- Be ready for further development and eventual production deployment.

**Your responsibility is to investigate, understand, decide, design, implement, test, and refine.**

Do not transfer the research responsibility to me.

Do not ask me to choose every section, color, component, or layout.

Use your own investigation and engineering judgment to make the best decisions, while respecting the actual Weechy product documentation.

Build something that Lark Player could not be mistaken for.

Build the official Weechy website.
